text: BTC looking close to resuming its uptrend. The fact we weathered as much bad press as we did while having minimal PA impact has spoken volumes. I was having a discussion with a normie friend explaining why I always see war fud as providing a pico bottom majority of the time. I'll give my left curve thesis. When there's no conflict among nations, the world is in harmony. Countries trade without restrictions, everybody is more or less an ally which means business is at its highest turnover/efficiency. When considering global GDP and economic output, these are your ideal conditions as everyone is maximizing turnover since there's no external fears. Reverse the roles and consider countries at war. Funding for innovation gets halted, government spending redirects to military equipment instead of advancing society, asset prices are targeted by opposing nations as one of the strongest ways to cause unrest in society, in turn fund managers and general sentiment reduces exposure to risk assets. When you look at a pendulum of world order when prices are strong, it usually falls into the first bucket. Prices generally top in "peak" euphoria, this might not necessarily mean that everyone is blindly bullish, it could simply mean that market participants are very unaware of any negative catalysts. Same principle for when we enter war, tariffs, inflation etc. Prices generally bottom on peak despair, maybe this isn't when everyone is the loudest (although it usually is) but when the market is so starved of positive catalyst that they can't see a reason for prices to trend up. Obviously this is a very broad approach to thinking and there's many nuances as any trader would know. I've been down the macro rabbit hole many times and while it's fun to try and have IQ battles with yourself understanding global supply chains, it's pretty likely your edge is minimal/non existent. B16z said something which I liked a lot along the lines of "you're better off leaning into left curve ideologies since the people on the right curve are extremely smart and you have no chance at competing with their way of thinking". Most of you reading this would benefit from doing the same. You aren't going to make life changing money from macro. Yes its an important factor of understanding what type of cycle we're in and looking for warning signs, although you're much better off putting 95% of your energy into strategies which can move the needle (AI coding, wallet tracking, researching potential future narratives, content production, testing products/airdrop farming etc). One thing I continually notice is how easy it is to become undisciplined with your time as discourse on CT, podcasts, GC's can flood your brain with instant gratification. When you sit down, lock your phone away and set a timer for 3 hours, its incredible how much deep work you can get done when you're generally interested in something that can increase skills or ability to make money. Time spent worrying about majors or macro should be kept to a minimum, my best routine is going deep for a few days and crafting a thesis for how I see the next 2-4 weeks playing out. Write a few key validations/invalidations then carry on with whatever the most impactful task will be to my portfolio and long term skillset. For the past few weeks I've mentioned how I'm bullish at these price levels, except it's clear there hasn't been a catalyst that would bring a meaningful reversal. While I still don't think it's clear yet, defending recent price levels against the security fud was quite noteworthy. As AI progresses, many industries will continue to become irrelevant. The longer BTC and crypto stick around against things like legacy software, the greater the Lindy effect and narrative of "AI winner" becomes. Key area I'm watching on low time frame is daily close above 84.5k. We've had volatility compression for quite some time with strong sentiment reversion over the past 3-5 days, ETF's did half a billion on Monday. I think the trend continues up within the next week or so.

text: OCC Finalizes First GENIUS Act Rule: No Safe Harbor for Existing Stablecoin Rewards The OCC has issued its first final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, covering stablecoin issuance, custody, and third-party partnerships, effective January 18, 2027. Existing yield and rewards programs receive no automatic grandfathering or safe harbor; compliance will be assessed case by case. The act prohibits issuers from paying yield solely for holding, using, or retaining stablecoins, but does not ban all third-party rewards. The OCC said rewards based at least partly on other factors may fall outside the prohibition. The implications for programs offered by Coinbase, PayPal, and Kraken remain uncertain. — link

text: ZachXBT: Institution Suspected of Losing $2.84M to North Korean Group SquidSquad On-chain investigator ZachXBT reported that an unnamed institution was suspected of being compromised on BNB Chain on October 8, losing roughly $2.84 million to North Korea-linked entity SquidSquad. According to his tracking, the attacker deposited 1,111.2 ETH into Tornado Cash on October 20, withdrew the funds across three addresses, and bridged the proceeds from Ethereum to Tron via USDT0. The funds were then aggregated into two addresses that show transaction linkages to wallets previously attributed to North Korea. Within minutes, the stolen assets were routed through intermediary addresses to Chinese OTC brokers, a tactic ZachXBT believes was intended to evade potential asset freezes by Tether. — link
